galaxies.title: Table of 2
galaxies.chapterCopy: Every orbit here carries its satellites in pairs — count by 2 and the rings fill in.

galaxies.title: Table of 3
galaxies.chapterCopy: Three to a ring: a loose belt of small worlds that only steadies when you count by 3.

galaxies.title: Table of 4
galaxies.chapterCopy: Four satellites ride each ring — half of eight, twice two, and always an even chart.

galaxies.title: Table of 5
galaxies.chapterCopy: Five-pointed and handy: rings of five line up with your hands.

galaxies.title: Table of 6
galaxies.chapterCopy: Six per ring turns slowly under a steady skip-count — half a dozen, again and again.

galaxies.title: Table of 7
galaxies.chapterCopy: Seven is the first odd drift that feels far away — lock it and the whole chart calms.

galaxies.title: Table of 8
galaxies.chapterCopy: Eight to a ring: double four, and the fastest way is to take a known ring twice.

galaxies.title: Table of 9
galaxies.chapterCopy: Nine sits one shy of ten — build it as a full ring minus one and it stops slipping.

galaxies.title: Table of 10
galaxies.chapterCopy: Tens chart themselves: add a ring, add a zero, keep your place.

galaxies.title: Table of 11
galaxies.chapterCopy: Eleven plays a trick: up by eleven each ring — until ten rings make it a hundred and ten.

galaxies.title: Table of 12
galaxies.chapterCopy: The deep field: twelve to a ring, dozens at a glance — the boss chart of the atlas.
